title: Deletion queue DAGs: deletes_job → cleanup sweep → PG drain
answers: How does the person deletion queue DAG work?
How do tombstoned persons get removed from Postgres?
body:
- posthog/dags/deletes.py:`deletes_job` (~L1153) processes pending AsyncDeletion rows (events, then person, person_distinct_id2, groups).
- posthog/dags/clickhouse_cleanup.py:`run_cleanup_sweep_after_deletes` (run_status_sensor) launches the sweep when deletes_job succeeds, skipping if one is active.
- `clickhouse_deletion_sweep_job` ops chained by output to serialize cluster mutations: clear_removed_cohort_data → snapshot_deleted_persons → snapshot_orphaned_distinct_ids → recheck (before distinct id delete) → delete_orphaned_distinct_ids → recheck (before person delete) → persist_deleted_persons → delete_persons → publish_sweep_metrics → drop_snapshot_assets.
- Why snapshots: the sweep destroys the tombstones its worklist derives from, so the worklist is frozen in run-id-scoped snapshot tables; the recheck ops exclude revived persons.
- Job tag `clickhouse_deletion_sweep_concurrency: v1` relies on a run-queue limit of 1 in charts; max_runtime 43200.
- Sweep queues persons into person_pg_cleanup_queue; posthog/dags/person_pg_cleanup_drain.py drains it via personhog DeleteTombstonedPersons, which only deletes persons still tombstoned (queue is advisory; persons may be revived).
